best_for: Indie and hobby game developers who want a small, free 2D and 3D engine with no royalties, and who are fine scripting in GDScript or C#.
description:
Godot is a free, open-source engine for making 2D and 3D games, developed in the open by its community and supported by the Godot Foundation through donations and sponsors.

You build a game from nodes, small building blocks you combine into scenes and reuse. Your own data, such as characters or items, can be saved as resources and assigned to nodes right in the editor. 2D games get a dedicated renderer that works in real pixel coordinates. 3D renderers include Direct3D 12 and Metal, and OpenXR and WebXR support is built in for VR and AR. C++ code plugs in through GDExtension without recompiling the engine, and community bindings add languages such as Rust, Python and JavaScript.

points.title: MIT license, your game is yours
points.text: Godot is free under the MIT license, including for commercial games. The license does not cover what you make with it, so you own your game. If you ship the engine, include its copyright notice, for example in your credits.

points.title: No installer to run
points.text: The editor is self-contained: unzip it and run it. The Windows downloads here come as zips for x86, x64 and Arm64, and the macOS build is one universal zip for Intel and Apple silicon.

points.title: C# is a separate download
points.text: Godot offers a standard build and a .NET build. Only the .NET build runs C#, and it needs the .NET SDK installed. Godot sold on Steam, itch.io and the Epic Games Store has no C# support, and C# does not export to the web in Godot 4.

points.title: Graphics needs are modest
points.text: Vulkan 1.0 hardware is recommended; OpenGL 3.3 or OpenGL ES 3.0 is the minimum. Exporting to other platforms needs the matching export templates, standard or .NET.

points.title: Consoles go through partners
points.text: Desktop, mobile and web exports are built in. Console releases are handled by third-party publishers rather than the Godot project.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is a community build
points.text: The Flatpak for x64 and Arm64 is not verified, and Flathub says it is not affiliated with the Godot developers. It lacks C#; that needs a separate GodotSharp package.

points.title: Many versions on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 65 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source. Projects often stay on one engine version until they ship.
